g.text: Where the mess is in Card Cleaner
2026-11-21 | v1 | TychoHenzen/cardcleaner @ e458b795 (master), for the repo owner
Our repo drawn as our own card shop: every yellow tag marks a mess, and the numbers match the cards and the cleaning list.

g.title: The repo as our card shop, seen from above

g.data-maps-to: Assets/ .godot/ .code-review-graph/ .Serena/ floorplan/ addons/gdUnit4 addons/asset_manager addons/godot_ai addons/saveable addons/tile_editor
g.title: Not part of this map
g.desc: These are big, but they are someone else's code or a tool's own cache. Leaving them off this map is the author's scope choice. Only the project's own patches and autoloads inside them are counted above.

g.aria-label: sees the shop half as one lump
g.title: sees the shop half as one lump
g.desc: All Godot node classes are one UI module, so the hand, shelves and checkout are never checked against each other.

g.title: Core is mostly tile loading
g.desc: 61 of the 71 files in Core/Services load tiles, atlases, TMX or Wang sets, which only the map generators and the tile editor use. 22 Core files import Deckbuilder.Tiles, so shared code depends on a feature.
g.text: Core: 61 of 71 service files load tiles

g.aria-label: tile loading serves the maps and the tile editor
g.title: tile loading serves the maps and the tile editor
g.desc: The tile, atlas and Wang loading in Core is used by the map pipelines and the tile editor only.

g.aria-label: Two map pipelines in two homes
g.title: Two map pipelines in two homes
g.desc: The square-grid generator lives under Deckbuilder, the irregular mesh (about 5,500 lines) under Worldgen. Both are reachable. Worldgen is the biggest folder (15,071 lines) but saw almost no change in November. Keeping both is an owner decision.
g.text: two map makers, two homes: keep both?

g.title: The cellar: leftovers nobody opens
g.desc: A 312 MB Python environment for a January prototype; the prototype itself (1,501 lines) and 11 images (21 MB) still tracked in tools/; crash dumps and old logs at the root; a stale .quality folder; an old IDE test-runner chain; a context-export script; a 345-line waiver file nothing in the repo reads.

g.title: Legacy and dead code
g.desc: StartScene is no longer the main scene but three tests hold it in place. Two legacy save classes (172 lines, 452 lines of tests) serve a game with no released saves, though CLAUDE.md keeps one on purpose. OrderTerminal is a second ordering screen used only in the workshop. A few tile helpers are dead or used only by tests.

g.aria-label: The gate is green but cannot see the shop
g.title: The gate is green but cannot see the shop
g.desc: Every gated number is at its floor (no upward edges, no loop, no leaky seam). But all 241 Godot node classes form one UI module, so no loop inside the shop half can show. The gate builds its class map from its own Roslyn compile of Scripts/, which reported 83 errors in a local run on 2026-11-19 and carries on; the game itself builds. 69 of 92 interfaces have exactly one implementation.

g.aria-label: One click, six folders, three move rules
g.title: One click, six folders, three move rules
g.desc: One click passes through about 20 small files in six folders. The 'one move rule' has three paths: records, a cardboard box moved as a body, and an open box held as the source. The box exception is restated in five files, and three click targets stub IInteractable with CanInteract => false so a type switch can decide for them.

g.aria-label: Shop folder: ten topics in one heap
g.title: Shop folder: ten topics in one heap
g.desc: 197 files and 13,051 lines sorted by file kind (Components 58, Models 87 flat, Services 33, Ui 19), so one topic touches four folders. Shelf code also sits in Card (DeckSlot) and the whole-game save sits under Card.

g.title: CLAUDE.md re-describes the code
g.desc: 116 KB and 950 lines. About 70 percent describes current classes, about 16 percent is incident history, about 13 percent is commands and rules. 80 of the 329 commits since November 1 had to touch it. Several statements are already stale.

g.aria-label: Old plans on the notice board
g.title: Old plans on the notice board
g.desc: 9,043 lines of docs, 5,136 of them map-generation plans and questionnaires from October whose names partly no longer exist in the code. openspec/specs is empty and its config is the untouched template.

g.aria-label: Test rig bigger than what it tests
g.title: Test rig bigger than what it tests
g.desc: The runner's fixture is 1,514 lines for an 814-line runner. 33 suites write their own wait helper beside the shared BoundedWait. Engine and vendor workarounds each carry a pin test and prose with no stated exit. The repo patches its own scanner instead of fixing it at the source.

g.title: every run delivers a folder
g.desc: Each local runner or e2e run writes a new folder under reports/, and no step ever removes one.

g.title: The delivery area is full
g.desc: About 2 GB in about 750 run folders since 2026-10-03, most named after one ticket or one bisect step. The runner keeps every report (-rc 100000) and nothing ever deletes a folder. Git ignores the folder, so it never shows up.

g.aria-label: Test code compiles into the game
g.title: Test code compiles into the game
g.desc: gdUnit runs C# tests inside Godot, so Tests/ must compile into the game assembly: that part is the price of in-engine tests. The gap is that nothing leaves tests, Roslyn, FsCheck and NSubstitute out of an exported build, and the AI-editor helper autoload starts with the game. Whether an export carries them is not verified.

delete .venv-poc and the dumps at the
